findings.title: getSubGroupsCount contract change may break callers expecting non-null
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the underlying group model cannot be loaded (modelSupplier.get() returns null), whereas previously it would throw an NPE calling getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(). Callers of GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount() (e.g. GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount which does representation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())) may not expect a null Long and could behave unexpectedly (e.g. silently showing no count, or NPE if later code unboxes the value). This silently changes the method's contract without updating callers or documenting the new null-return semantics.

findings.title: Test spawns thread with no join/cleanup and busy-loops without any delay or timeout
findings.body: The new createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti test starts a background thread that tightly loops calling groups() until deletedAll is set, but never joins the thread or verifies it has actually finished before the test method returns. If the background thread throws an exception after the main thread exits (e.g., during the final iteration), it's recorded into caughtExceptions but the assertion may run before the thread observes deletedAll and exits, causing flakiness. There's also no timeout/retry bound, so a stuck condition could hang resources indefinitely across test runs sharing the JVM. The lack of thread.join() means the test can finish while the reader thread is still running, polluting subsequent tests or causing non-deterministic failures.
